# SolarSized

> Free solar and battery sizing: daily kWh to panel watts, battery kWh and inverter size, using NREL PVWatts peak sun hours by state.

Panel W = daily Wh / (sun hours x 0.75). Battery kWh = daily Wh x days / (0.9 x 0.9).

## Start here
- [Calculator](https://solarsized.com/)
- [Methodology](https://solarsized.com/methodology/)
- [About SolarSized](https://solarsized.com/about/): who publishes the site (EYEVUE Ventures), how the numbers are made, contact eyevueventures@gmail.com.
- [Privacy policy](https://solarsized.com/privacy/): cookieless Cloudflare Web Analytics, no accounts; an optional real-world test submission form (data + proof photo/link stored in Cloudflare, email optional and never published), affiliate cookies set only on the retailer's site, no sale of data. Effective 2026-10-27.
- [Submit a real-world test](https://solarsized.com/submit-test/): proof-required, consented form for a reader's own measured production. The URL stays available to people, is noindex, follow, and is not in the sitemap. It is not a public results page. Entries are reviewed by hand; verified results are published on the matching guide or state page as "Verified owner test" data.
- [Affiliate disclosure](https://solarsized.com/disclosure/): Amazon Associates links, labeled and marked rel="sponsored".
- [Peak sun hours by state](https://solarsized.com/states/)
- [Appliances](https://solarsized.com/appliances/)
- [Data: states.json](https://solarsized.com/data/states.json)

## Guides
- [How many solar panels do I need? State-by-state sizing guide](https://solarsized.com/guides/how-many-solar-panels-do-i-need/): The average U.S. home used 863 kWh a month in 2024. Divide your yearly kWh by your state's PVWatts output per kW: that is 10–27 400 W panels for the average home, depending on the state. Full table, worked examples, batteries and FAQ.
- [How much battery storage do I need? Home battery sizing in kWh and kW](https://solarsized.com/guides/how-much-battery-storage-do-i-need/): Size a home battery for kWh (how long) and kW plus surge amps (what runs). Essentials: about 4.5 kWh a day; average home: about 32 kWh. Outage tables, winter recharge, Powerwall 3 vs aPower 2 vs IQ 5P.
- [Does a home battery pay for itself on time-of-use rates? Payback math for PG&E, SCE and DTE](https://solarsized.com/guides/home-battery-payback-time-of-use/): One 13.5 kWh battery cycled daily at $15,647 installed (EnergySage Jul 2026; older $13,473 kept as sensitivity). PG&E EV2-A ~$986/yr (~16 yr); SCE TOU-D-PRIME ~$1,012/yr (~15 yr); SCE TOU-D-4-9PM ~$751/yr (~21 yr); DTE Overnight Savers ~$480/yr (~33 yr); DTE D1.11 and PG&E E-TOU-C effectively never. Solar+NBT export-avoidance case ~$1,684/yr (~9 yr) at 5¢ exports. 25D residential credit ended after 2025.
- [Off-grid cabin solar sizing: panels, batteries and the winter math](https://solarsized.com/guides/off-grid-cabin/): Size for the worst month using PVGIS-NSRDB monthly output for 10 cabin regions (Marquette MI December 1.67 kWh/kW/day at a 62° tilt vs 4.41 near Flagstaff). Example loads from ENERGY STAR and maker specs: weekend cabin 1,568 Wh/day needs about 1.1 kW year-round in the U.P. (0.5 kW May–Sep); full-time cabin 4,057 Wh/day (full fridge, freezer, all-day Starlink Mini, Victron 11 W inverter idle) needs about 2.9 kW and 16 kWh LiFePO4 for 3 days (80% DoD). LiFePO4 can't charge below 32°F (EG4); generator refill via a 35 A 48 V charger. Portland latitude-tilt December (1.46 kWh/kW/day, checked Nov 6, 2026) is a west-side pointer on the guide; Bend stays in the 10-region table.
- [RV solar sizing: watts and battery for boondocking](https://solarsized.com/guides/rv-solar/): PVGIS-NSRDB worst-month output for flat roof panels vs tilted at 9 RV destinations by season (Quartzsite Dec 2.41 flat vs 4.37 kWh/kW/day tilted at 34°, +81%; summer flat beats tilt). Example loads from maker specs: weekender 1,000 Wh/day (absorption fridge on LP, MaxxFan, CPAP) needs ~500 W flat for a Quartzsite winter and ~200 Ah LiFePO4; full-timer 2,700 Wh/day (Dometic DMC4101 ~50 Ah/day, Starlink Mini, Victron Phoenix 12 W idle, CPAP with humidifier 55 W) needs ~1,250 W flat or ~700 W tilted plus ~470 Ah. Battle Born 100 A continuous / 32°F charge cutoff; Orion-Tr 12/12-30 adds 1.4–1.7 kWh per 4 h drive; 13.5K roof AC (~1,800 W) needs shore power or a generator.
- [Grid-tie vs battery backup: does solar work in a power outage?](https://solarsized.com/guides/grid-tie-vs-backup/): IEEE 1547-2018 requires grid-tied inverters to cease energizing within 2 s of an island (5 min return-to-service). Seven backup options compared: SMA Secure Power Supply (2,000 W outlet, daytime only), Enphase Sunlight Backup (IQ8 + System Controller 2, 4×240 V/8×120 V circuits, daytime only), partial-home battery (~$15,647 per 13.5 kWh, EnergySage Jul 2026), whole-home (~$34,000), generator, power station. PVGIS hourly 2005–2015 recharge for a 7 kW array in outage months: Houston Jul bad (10th-pct) day 18.6 kWh, Tampa Oct 19.3, Sacramento Oct 19.7, Asheville Sep 9.1, Dallas Feb 6.5, Denver Dec 7.1, Detroit/Boston Jan 2.6 vs 4.6 kWh needed for a 4.08 kWh/day essentials list. Powerwall 3 / IQ 5P / aPower 2 specs (185 A LRA), AC vs DC coupling, EIA 2024 SAIDI 662.6 min, 30% credit ended 2026-01-01.
- [Battery chemistry: LiFePO4 vs NMC vs lead-acid](https://solarsized.com/guides/battery-chemistry/): Decision guide with maker datasheets. LiFePO4 default for home/off-grid/RV: Battle Born BB10012 100% usable DoD and 3,000–5,000 deep cycles; EG4 LL-S >7,000 cycles at 80% DoD, charge from 32°F, UL 1973; Tesla Powerwall 3 LFP 13.5 kWh with UL 1973/9540/9540A and 10-yr 70% retention (unlimited cycles for solar/TOU/backup); Enphase IQ 5P LFP 5.0 kWh, warranty 15 yr or 6,000 cycles. Lead-acid: Trojan recommends ≤50% DoD (80% max safe); Premium flooded ~1,600 cycles @50%, AGM/gel ~1,000, Solar AGM ~1,700, Industrial ~2,800. NMC still for weight-critical portable packs (often ~500 cycles to ~80% on older stations). UL 1973=pack, UL 9540=system, UL 9540A=fire-propagation test method. EnergySage Jul 2026 ~$15,647 per 13.5 kWh install.
